name: Chemicals
one_liner: Converting oil, gas and minerals into materials used across nearly every industry, split between cyclical commodity chemicals and higher-margin specialties.
how_it_makes_money: Commodity producers sell high-volume basic chemicals and plastics where margins track the spread between feedstock and product prices. Specialty chemical makers sell performance-based formulations such as coatings, adhesives and additives, priced on value to the customer. Industrial gas companies earn steady returns from long-term supply contracts.
revenue_formula: Commodity margin = volume × (product price − feedstock cost) × plant utilization
Specialty revenue = customers × application volume × value-based price
cost_structure: Raw materials and feedstock: typically the largest cost, especially for commodities
Energy: natural gas and power for heat-intensive processes
Plant fixed costs and maintenance, with utilization driving unit cost
R&D and technical service: significant for specialties
margins: Commodity chemical margins are volatile and follow feedstock spreads and utilization, while specialty and industrial gas players earn steadier, higher margins. Feedstock advantage, scale, differentiation and customer switching costs drive the spread.

key_metrics.name: Capacity utilization
key_metrics.what: Share of plant capacity in use; drives fixed-cost absorption and pricing power.

key_metrics.name: Feedstock spread
key_metrics.what: Product price minus raw material cost, the core commodity profit driver.

key_metrics.name: EBITDA margin
key_metrics.what: Standard profitability measure, used to compare commodity and specialty players.

key_metrics.name: Price/volume/mix
key_metrics.what: Decomposition of revenue change, standard in chemicals reporting.

key_metrics.name: R&D intensity
key_metrics.what: R&D as share of sales, indicates specialty positioning.

key_metrics.name: Return on capital employed (ROCE)
key_metrics.what: Returns on large asset bases, key in a capital-heavy sector.

trends: Global overcapacity, especially from new Chinese capacity, pressuring commodity margins
Portfolio reshaping: spin-offs of commodity units and focus on specialties
US ethane feedstock advantage versus higher-cost European producers
PFAS and regulatory scrutiny creating liability and substitution demand
Weak demand in construction, autos and durables weighing on volumes
